source.title: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work
source.author: Ape to Gentleman

tips.text: Build colour pairings on contrast between a light shade and a dark one.
tips.why: Light-dark contrast is what most reliable combinations have in common.

tips.text: In a black and white outfit, aim for about 70/30: one piece in one colour and the rest in the other, rather than alternating pieces head to toe.
tips.why: Alternating black and white items looks like zebra stripes.

tips.text: Try navy with cream for smart casual outfits, such as an unstructured navy blazer with cream chinos.
tips.why: It has the contrast of black and white but feels softer.

tips.text: For autumn and winter, wear brown with beige as a tonal pairing, such as brown outerwear over beige trousers.
tips.why: The two shades sit together naturally in the colder months.

tips.text: Break up a brown and beige outfit with white, or a touch of muted green or burnt orange.
tips.why: A small contrast stops a tonal look from going flat.

tips.text: Pair dark green with black, especially in tailoring, for example a green blazer over a black roll neck for cocktail attire.
tips.why: Two dark colours together look rich and evening-appropriate.

tips.text: Use olive with white in summer, dressed up with tailoring or down with a tee and cargo trousers.
tips.why: The pairing is fresh and works at both ends of the formality scale.

tips.text: When combining brown and green, add white accents such as white sneakers.
tips.why: Without some white the earthy pairing can look dull and dated.

tips.text: For an easy low-risk outfit, mix different shades of grey, starting with dark charcoal against light grey.
tips.why: Greys always sit together; the shade difference keeps it interesting.

tips.text: Wear pink with blue in pale or pastel shades for casual spring and summer looks, not in the most saturated tones.
tips.why: Bright versions of the two colours tend to clash.
